title: 8 Best Datarails Alternatives for FP&A Teams in 2026
summary: Compare the 8 best Datarails alternatives in 2026, from Cube and Vena to AI agents like Concourse, by fit, features, and cost. Find the right FP&A tool for your team.
body_markdown:
Datarails is one of the better-liked FP&A platforms on the market. It works on top of Excel rather than asking your team to abandon it, pulling data from your ERP and other systems into a single source of truth while your analysts keep modeling in the spreadsheets they already know. That approach earns it a[4.6 out of 5 across hundreds of G2 reviews](https://www.g2.com/products/datarails/reviews) . So why do so many teams end up searching for **Datarails alternatives** ?


Usually because the same Excel-native design that makes Datarails easy to adopt is what teams eventually run into: spreadsheet performance and version control as models grow, a fit that skews toward small and mid-market teams, and implementations that take longer than expected. This guide compares the eight best Datarails alternatives in 2026, from spreadsheet-native peers like Cube to enterprise planning platforms like Anaplan, plus the newer wave of AI agents that *execute* FP&A work rather than just give you another place to build models.


## **What are the best Datarails alternatives?**


> The best Datarails alternatives in 2026 are Concourse for teams that want AI agents to run FP&A work end to end, Cube and Vena for spreadsheet-native FP&A, Planful for multi-entity consolidation, Pigment and Anaplan for enterprise planning, and Abacum and Prophix for modern mid-market CPM.


> **Concourse is the AI-agent alternative on this list.** Instead of another modeling surface you build in, Concourse deploys autonomous finance agents that connect to your ERP, data warehouse, and billing data to run forecasting, variance and flux analysis, board reporting, and ad hoc analysis end to end, with every number traceable back to source. It is built for finance teams that want AI to do the work, not just visualize it.


## **Why teams look for Datarails alternatives**


Datarails is a strong fit for its core buyer. The friction tends to show up as a team grows past that profile.


**The Excel foundation cuts both ways.** Building on spreadsheets is what makes Datarails approachable, but it also inherits Excel's limits: performance can degrade on large data sets, formula links break, and version control gets harder as more people touch the models. These are among the most common themes in[user reviews and comparisons](https://www.cubesoftware.com/blog/datarails-reviews) .


**It is built for small and mid-market teams.** Reviewers consistently place Datarails in the SMB to lower-mid-market range. Teams with complex, multi-entity consolidation or heavy cross-functional modeling often find they need a heavier platform, as noted across[FP&A comparison guides](https://www.venasolutions.com/blog/datarails-alternatives) .


**Implementation and learning curve.** Getting Datarails fully stood up commonly runs a few months, and the learning curve is steeper than a quick demo suggests. For a lean team, that time-to-value matters.


The point is not that Datarails is a weak product. It is that "well-liked" and "right for your team as it is now" are different questions. For a broader view of the category, see our roundup of the[best AI tools for FP&A](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/best-ai-tools-fpa-2025) .


## **How we evaluated Datarails alternatives**


FP&A tools are not interchangeable. A 30-person startup and a global enterprise need very different things. We compared the alternatives across six criteria that actually change the decision for a finance team.


- **Spreadsheet experience.** Whether it keeps you in Excel or Google Sheets, or moves you into a dedicated modeling UI, and how well it handles the transition.
- **Modeling and planning depth.** How far it scales, from lightweight budgeting to complex, multi-dimensional, cross-functional planning.
- **Consolidation.** Multi-entity and multi-currency close and consolidation, the place many teams outgrow Datarails.
- **Reporting and dashboards.** How easily you can produce board-ready reporting and explain the numbers behind it.
- **AI capability.** From a conversational assistant over your data to autonomous agents that execute the work.
- **Fit and time-to-value.** Ideal company size and how long implementation takes.

## **The 8 best Datarails alternatives in 2026**


### **1. Concourse, Best for AI Agents That Execute FP&A Work**


Concourse is an AI agent platform for corporate finance. Rather than give you another surface to build models in, it connects directly to your ERP, data warehouse, and billing data and runs FP&A workflows autonomously or on triggers: building and refreshing forecasts, running variance and flux analysis, answering ad hoc questions across your stack, and producing board and management reporting on a schedule.


What sets it apart from a modeling-first tool like Datarails is the execution model. Concourse does not just centralize your data for an analyst to work in. Its agents own the work end to end, and every output traces back to source data and is validated against evals built for your business, which answers finance's biggest objection to AI: whether you can defend the number to a board or an auditor. It meets teams where they already work, inside ChatGPT, Claude, Slack, Teams, and email, and exports to Excel, PowerPoint, and Google Sheets. Concourse reports customer results including a 75% reduction in manual work and 20+ hours saved per user per month, is SOC 2 Type II certified, and connects to 100+ systems including NetSuite, QuickBooks, Snowflake, Salesforce, and Stripe.


**Best for.** Finance teams that want AI agents to actually run forecasting, variance, and reporting, with full traceability, rather than another tool to build models in.


**Keep in mind.** Concourse is an execution and analysis layer, not a spreadsheet modeling UI. If your team's core need is hand-building complex models in a grid, use Concourse to run the analysis and reporting on top rather than as a like-for-like Datarails swap.


### **2. Cube, Best Spreadsheet-Native Alternative**


Cube is the closest like-for-like alternative to Datarails: a spreadsheet-native FP&A platform that layers a centralized data model under both Excel *and* Google Sheets, so teams can run month-end, variance, and board reporting without leaving the spreadsheet. Cube has raised[roughly $65 million to date](https://www.finsmes.com/2022/06/cube-closes-30m-series-b-funding.html) , including a $30 million Series B led by Battery Ventures.


**Best for.** Fast-scaling startups and mid-market teams with lean FP&A headcount that want a modern layer without leaving spreadsheets.


**Keep in mind.** It is still spreadsheet-centric, so very complex multi-entity or enterprise modeling can eventually outgrow it.


### **3. Vena Solutions, Best for Excel-Native FP&A with Governance**


Vena is another Excel-native platform, but with more structure and governance than Datarails, built on its own modeling engine and paired with the Vena Copilot AI assistant. It removes the version-control and error problems of raw spreadsheets while keeping teams in a familiar interface. Vena has[raised around $476 million](https://sacra.com/c/vena/) , including a $300 million round led by Vista Equity Partners, and serves 900+ customers.


**Best for.** Mid-market to lower-enterprise finance teams committed to Microsoft and Excel that need more governance than Datarails offers.


**Keep in mind.** It is heavier and more structured, so templating and implementation can be more involved.


### **4. Planful, Best for Multi-Entity Consolidation**


Planful is a cloud FP&A and CPM platform whose standout strength is multi-entity, multi-currency consolidation and close, alongside budgeting, forecasting, and reporting. It is a common step up for teams that outgrow a spreadsheet-native tool specifically because their consolidation needs got real.


**Best for.** Mid-size to large finance teams with genuine multi-entity consolidation requirements.


**Keep in mind.** Reviewers suggest buying it for consolidation strength rather than AI, which is still maturing relative to the newer platforms.


### **5. Pigment, Best for AI-Native Enterprise Planning**


Pigment is an AI-native, multi-dimensional planning platform known for strong modeling and a modern interface, often cross-shopped as a contemporary Anaplan alternative. Founded in Paris in 2019, it[raised a $145 million Series D in 2024](https://techcrunch.com/2024/04/04/business-planning-startup-pigment-raises-145-million-round-in-rare-french-tech-megaround/) led by ICONIQ Growth, reaching a $1 billion valuation.


**Best for.** Growth to enterprise companies that want modern, integrated planning across finance and functions like sales and workforce.


**Keep in mind.** It carries more platform and implementation weight than a spreadsheet tool, and sits at a premium price point.


### **6. Anaplan, Best for Enterprise Connected Planning**


Anaplan is the enterprise heavyweight for connected planning across FP&A, supply chain, and sales at massive scale. Taken private by[Thoma Bravo for roughly $10.7 billion in 2022](https://www.thomabravo.com/press-releases/anaplan-to-be-acquired-by-thoma-bravo-for-10.7-billion) , it is built for large, global organizations with complex, cross-functional planning and the IT resources to run it.


**Best for.** Large and global enterprises with complex, cross-functional planning needs.


**Keep in mind.** It is the heaviest and most expensive option here, and overkill for the SMB and mid-market teams Datarails typically serves. It is the opposite end of the spectrum.


### **7. Abacum, Best for Modern Mid-Market Planning**


Abacum is an AI-powered business planning platform that consolidates financial and operational data for forecasting, scenario modeling, headcount planning, and automated reporting, with a collaborative, modern feel. It[raised a $60 million Series B in 2025](https://www.builtinnyc.com/articles/abacum-raises-60m-series-b-20250612) led by Scale Venture Partners.


**Best for.** Mid-market finance teams that want a modern, collaborative planning tool.


**Keep in mind.** It is younger and smaller than the incumbents, with its deepest traction in the mid-market rather than large enterprise.


### **8. Prophix, Best for Unified Mid-Market CPM**


Prophix offers unified corporate performance management for the mid-market, combining budgeting, forecasting, consolidation, close, and reporting in a single platform (Prophix One). Founded in Canada in 1987 with 3,000+ customers, it is often the "more than spreadsheets, less than enterprise CPM" pick from a single vendor and data model.


**Best for.** Mid-size companies that want one platform for the full CPM cycle rather than stitching tools together.


**Keep in mind.** It has a more traditional CPM feel, and reviewers often cite it as the safe pick rather than the most modern or AI-forward UX.


*A note on Mosaic:* you will still see mosaic.tech on older "Datarails alternatives" lists. Mosaic was[acquired by HiBob in 2025](https://www.hibob.com/news/hibob-acquires-financial-planning-and-analysis-platform-mosaic-expanding-capabilities-to-empower-people-first-cfos/) and folded into its HR platform, so it is no longer sold as a standalone FP&A tool. We have left it off the list for that reason.


## **Which Datarails alternative is right for you?**


There is no single best Datarails alternative, only the best fit for your size, stack, and biggest bottleneck. The short version:


- **Choose Concourse** if you want AI agents to *execute* FP&A work, from forecasting and variance to board reporting, with every number traceable and audit-ready.
- **Choose Cube** if you want the closest spreadsheet-native experience to Datarails, across Excel and Google Sheets.
- **Choose Vena** if you are committed to Excel but need more governance and structure.
- **Choose Planful** if multi-entity consolidation is the reason you are leaving.
- **Choose Pigment** if you want AI-native, modern enterprise planning across functions.
- **Choose Anaplan** if you are a large enterprise with complex connected-planning needs.
- **Choose Abacum** if you want a modern, collaborative mid-market planning tool.
- **Choose Prophix** if you want unified mid-market CPM from a single vendor.


The clearest shift in 2026 is the split between tools that give you a better place to *build* the plan and tools that *do* the work for you. Most of this list is the former. The AI-agent layer is the latter, and increasingly teams pair a planning tool with an agent that runs the forecasting, variance, and reporting on top.


## **Frequently asked questions**


### **What is the best alternative to Datarails?**


It depends on why you are leaving. Cube is the closest spreadsheet-native peer, Planful leads for multi-entity consolidation, and Pigment or Anaplan for enterprise modeling. For teams that want AI agents to actually run FP&A workflows such as forecasting, variance, and reporting, all with audit-ready traceability, Concourse is the strongest AI-agent alternative.


### **Is there a cheaper alternative to Datarails?**


Datarails is quote-based, with third-party trackers like[Vendr](https://www.vendr.com/buyer-guides/datarails) estimating it starts around $24,000 per year and that typical small-team deals land in the $25,000 to $50,000 range. Most alternatives, including Cube, Abacum, and Concourse, also use custom pricing, so expect a scoped quote rather than a public list price. Lighter, modern tools generally deploy faster than heavier CPM suites.


### **What is the best Datarails alternative for small teams?**


Small and lean finance teams typically look at Cube or Abacum for modern, quick-to-deploy planning, and increasingly at AI-agent platforms like Concourse to run forecasting, variance, and reporting without building and maintaining models by hand.


### **How is an AI agent different from an FP&A tool like Datarails?**


An FP&A platform like Datarails is where you build and store the plan: it centralizes data into a model and helps a person budget, forecast, and report. An AI agent platform like Concourse is a layer that executes the work across your existing systems, pulling data, running the analysis, and producing the deliverable, with a human approving. One is where you model; the other does the work.


### **Does Concourse replace Datarails?**


For the FP&A work itself, forecasting, variance, and reporting, Concourse agents can produce those outputs directly from your source data. If your team specifically wants a spreadsheet modeling surface to hand-build models in, run Concourse on top of that. If your priority is getting the analysis and reporting done, Concourse can own those workflows.


## **The bottom line**


Datarails is a well-liked FP&A platform, but Excel-native design, an SMB and mid-market fit, and multi-month implementations push plenty of teams to look elsewhere. The right alternative depends on your scale and your biggest bottleneck, from Cube for a modern spreadsheet-native experience to Planful for consolidation to Anaplan at the enterprise tier.


The bigger shift is from software that gives you a better place to build the plan to software that does the work. If you want to see what AI agents can do across forecasting, variance analysis, and board reporting, all with every number traceable and board-ready,[book a demo of Concourse](https://www.concourse.ai/) and put an agent on your next forecast.
